archetype.name: Playoff Team (shooting-first)
archetype.definition: A Warriors team whose elite shot-making, led by Curry, carries a roughly league-average defense and a thin frontcourt into the upper half of the West, without yet playing like one of its very best teams.

report.headline: Curry and a league-best 3-point stroke outrun an ordinary defense
report.take:
Golden State is 7-3 and seventh on the site, a sharp reversal from a 37-45 season that ranked 20th. The record has a clear source: the offense. Its 118.5 offensive rating ranks 5th, its TS % of 60.6 ranks 2nd and its 3P % of 39.5 leads the league, 4.8 points above average, on a 3PA Rate of 47.1 that ranks 6th. The defense is ordinary. Its 113.5 defensive rating is 14th and sits right at the league mean. Net Rtg of 5 ranks only 12th, which tells you this is a good team rather than an elite one.

The engine is Stephen Curry. He has 250 points in 237 minutes on a 70.8 TS %, carries a 34.5 USG % and a 14.3 BPM, and ranks 2nd on his position's tab. The rest of the scoring comes from Yaxel Lendeborg, who leads the team in minutes and has 212 points on a 63 TS %, and a backcourt group that grades A-. The frontcourt grades D-. Draymond Green is running offense, with 62 assists, but scoring almost nothing: 23 points on a 40.2 TS %. The bigs behind him rank in the 40s and 50s on their tabs.

The numbers hide three things. First, the shooting is hotter than anything in recent history. The 39.5 from three tops every season back to 2021-22, and last year's mark was 35.6, so some regression is coming. Second, the defense has a structural quirk. It allows the fewest rim attempts in the league (Opp Rim Rate 22.4, 1st) but the second-worst finishing once opponents get there (71.2, 29th), and it gives up second chances (DRB % 71.2, 22nd). Third, the record is a fair reflection of the margin. W vs Pt Diff is just 1 and the differential implies 6 wins. The 5-0 run with only 107.8 allowed a game came entirely at home, and two of those wins came by three points and in overtime.

Going forward, this looks like a team that settles in as a solid playoff side rather than one riding a 57-win pace. That holds as long as Curry stays on the floor and the offense stays top-five, even after the threes cool. The open question is whether the defense's late surge is real or a home-schedule mirage, and the road trip ahead will test it.

strengths.title: Curry's historically efficient start
strengths.body: Curry has 250 points on a 70.8 TS % while using over a third of possessions, and his 14.3 BPM is the biggest individual number on the sheet. The efficiency will drift down from this level, but even a regressed Curry keeps a top-tier offense. The team leans on him heavily: he has played 8 of the 10 games.

strengths.title: Top-five offense built on threes
strengths.body: The offensive rating ranks 5th, behind an eFG % that ranks 2nd and the league's best 3P % on heavy volume. It also gets to the line more than usual (FT Rate 31.4, 7th) and crashes the offensive glass (ORB % 29.6, 8th). The volume and style are sustainable. The 39.5 percent clip probably isn't, since no recent Warriors season shot above 38.5.

strengths.title: Wings and backcourt carry real grades
strengths.body: The wings grade A+ and the backcourt A-, with Lendeborg 9th on his tab and Podziemski 12th. Podziemski's 13.1 On-Off and 59.7 TS % in a low-usage role make him the quiet glue. The wing grade rests almost entirely on Lendeborg, though. His -33.1 On-Off over ten games is the kind of small-sample noise not to read much into either way.

concerns.title: Frontcourt can't finish or protect
concerns.body: The frontcourt grades D-. Green's 40.2 TS % makes him a non-scorer, and the defense allows the second-worst Opp Rim FG % while ranking 22nd in DRB %. The scheme keeps opponents away from the rim, but the ones who get there score, and misses become second chances. Charles Bassey, with a 70.4 TS % and 19.6 On-Off in limited minutes, is the one big pointing the other way.

concerns.title: Shooting regression is coming
concerns.body: The 39.5 3P % leads the league and sits well above last season's 35.6 and every recent year on the sheet. With nearly half the shots coming from deep, a cooler stretch will move the offense more than it would for most teams. Expect the offensive rating to slide from 5th toward the edge of the top ten.

concerns.title: Turnovers and a middling defense
concerns.body: TOV % of 14.8 ranks 23rd, a point worse than the league. The defensive rating sits at the league mean, and the defense ranked 17th last year, so average is the honest baseline. The recent 107.8 points allowed a game came over five home games and shouldn't be treated as the new normal yet.

trend.note: It lost the first three games, then went on a seven-game winning streak, finishing October 3-3 and opening November 4-0. The last five came with the defense noticeably tighter, though all of them were at home and two were one-possession or overtime games.

weekAhead.headline: Pelicans twice bracket a hard road test in Houston, San Antonio
weekAhead.body:
The week is two halves. New Orleans, a 4-6 team ranked 18th with a 21st-ranked defense, comes in twice, once at home and once on the road. Its defense has been hammered by point guards (31.9 a game, 27th), which sets up well for Curry, and it barely shoots threes (3PA Rate 32, 30th). The catch is its A+ frontcourt and 3rd-ranked FT Rate, which aim straight at Golden State's weakest group and its leaky rim finishing.

In between come two road games against teams ranked above the Warriors on the site. Houston (net 9.3) has the league's 2nd-best Opp 3P % and an A+ frontcourt that hits the glass. San Antonio (net 10.3) has the 4th-best defensive rating, the 2nd-best rim defense, an A+ backcourt and the fewest turnovers in the league, so it won't feed off Golden State's giveaways the way it might want. A 3-1 week is realistic if the shooting travels; a split is the more likely floor.

keyMatchups.title: Curry against New Orleans' point-guard leak
keyMatchups.body: The Pelicans have allowed the most points over their own averages to point guards, 31.9 a game. Two games against that defense are the best scoring setup of the week for Curry. Both should be games Golden State is expected to win.

keyMatchups.title: Houston's perimeter defense versus the threes
keyMatchups.body: Houston holds opponents to a 31.6 3P %, 2nd in the league, and pairs it with a top-three offense. That is a direct test of whether Golden State's shooting is real or a hot stretch. The Rockets' 6th-ranked ORB % also targets the Warriors' weak defensive rebounding.

keyMatchups.title: San Antonio's guards and rim wall
keyMatchups.body: The Spurs' A+ backcourt meets a Warriors defense that gives up an outsized share of its points to shooting guards. Their 4th-ranked defense allows just 59.4 at the rim. On the road, this is the hardest game of the week.

weekAhead.watch: Whether the tighter defense of the home winning streak survives road trips to Houston and San Antonio.

restOfSeason.body:
The 57-win pace overstates things. A 12th-ranked Net Rtg, a league-leading 3P % that history says will cool, and a defense that has sat around league average for two seasons point to a team in the high 40s to low 50s in wins. The record isn't propped up by close-game luck, since the margin implies 6 of the 7 wins. The regression risk lies in the shot-making, not in fortune. Expect the offensive rating to settle somewhere around 115 to 118 and the 3P % to land in the 36.5 to 38.5 range.

The ceiling depends on Curry's availability and on whether the frontcourt can get better than D-. Bassey's productive minutes are one internal lever, and Green's playmaking keeps the offense humming even without scoring. The floor is protected by an offense that should stay top-ten. That makes this a likely playoff team, probably not a play-in one, but not yet a contender on its underlying numbers.
swingFactors: Frontcourt rim defense and defensive rebounding

confidence.note: Ten games, a shooting spike and a home-heavy streak.
